text: Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany.
Paris is the capital of France and sits on the Seine river.
Tokyo is the capital of Japan and one of the most populous metropolitan areas in the world.
Canberra, not Sydney, is the capital city of Australia.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure.
Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (32 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure.
The chemical symbol for gold is Au and for silver is Ag.
Mount Everest, located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and China, is Earth's highest mountain above sea level.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions.
The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries by successive Chinese dynasties to protect against invasions.
World War II ended in 1945 after the surrender of Germany in May and Japan in September.
The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.
The human body has 206 bones in adulthood.
DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, carries the genetic instructions used in the growth and functioning of living organisms.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 kilometers per second.
Earth orbits the Sun once approximately every 365.25 days, which is why calendars include a leap year every four years.
The Amazon rainforest, located primarily in Brazil, is the largest tropical rainforest in the world.
Albert Einstein developed the theory of general relativity, published in 1915.
The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.
Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language first released in 1991.
The internet's core protocol suite, TCP/IP, was standardized in the early 1980s.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, spanning much of North Africa.
The human heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
